FAQs

Everything you need to know about Creatives Takeover.

What is Creatives Takeover?

Creatives Takeover is a SaaS platform where founders and indie builders start and test their projects. It brings the tools for each stage into one workspace: defining your customer, testing demand, building a first version, planning your launch, measuring traction, and preparing to raise.

Around the tools you also have Pulse, an assistant that reads your project, plus mentors, cofounders, service providers and investors. The Rookie plan is free; some tools use monthly credits.

How does the Startup Development Cycle work?

It splits the work of building a startup into seven stages: Identity, Prototyping, Validation, Building, Launch, Traction and Fundraising. Each stage has a clear goal and the tools for it, for example ICP Builder for Identity, PMF Lab for Validation, MVP Builder for Building, and GTM Strategist and Traction Engine for Launch and Traction.

You don't have to follow it in order. Start at the stage that matches where your project is; your dashboard keeps the tasks and progress for each one.

I don't have a clear business idea yet. Can this platform still help me?

Yes. You can start with a rough idea. Describe it in the box at the top of this page and ICP Builder gives you a first assessment of who it could serve, before you create an account.

You can also explore business directions in the Prompt Library, work through a first plan with BizMap AI, and read Founder Stories to see how others started.

Is Creatives Takeover only for tech startups?

No. We built this for founders, indie hackers, and creative builders in general, not just traditional venture backed startups.

Freelancers, creators, consultants, educators, SaaS founders, service businesses, marketplace ideas, niche products, local businesses, and solo internet businesses can all use the platform.

If you are trying to build something real from scratch and want practical support instead of corporate jargon, you are exactly who this is for.

Is my business idea safe?

Yes. Your workspace is private by default, and we take idea confidentiality seriously.

Your data is protected with secure infrastructure, encryption, and access controls. We do not sell your idea, share it with other founders, or expose your private startup work unless you choose to share something yourself. We also do not use your private startup data as public showcase material for other users.

And to calm the bigger fear: startups are rarely won because someone heard an idea. They are won through execution, customer understanding, speed, and consistency. Our job is to help you move faster while keeping your work private.

How can I discover investors and funding opportunities?

Insighta groups the fundraising tools.

VC Search lets you browse and filter venture capital firms by industry, stage, location and check size. Every plan can browse; opening full profiles takes a paid plan: 5 a month on Starter, 10 on Rising, unlimited on Pro. Accelerator Hunt works the same way.

Pitch Deck Analyzer and Insighta Test help you prepare before you reach out, and Find Your Angel, on Pro, connects you with angel investors. We can't promise investment; these tools help you find the right people and prepare for the conversation.

Will I be working on my own?

No. Besides the tools, the platform connects you with people: mentors you can book for focused advice, a cofounder marketplace, service providers for sales, marketing, operations and tech support, and Rooms and Launchpad to work next to other founders. On Pro, Find Your Angel connects you with angel investors.

Your Founder ID gives you a public page to share your progress with all of them.

What tools help me validate my startup idea?

ICP Builder helps you define exactly who you are building for and what pain points matter most. PMF Lab helps you pressure test whether the market actually wants what you are making. BizMap AI helps you challenge your assumptions through conversation and turn research into action.

Together, these tools help you move from 'this sounds interesting' to 'there is real evidence worth building on.'

Who is behind Creatives Takeover and why should I trust the service?

We're a small team of founders, builders, and growth people who genuinely care about helping others launch what matters.

Javier Alonso (Founder and CEO) started this because he wanted to give ambitious builders a realistic path from idea to execution. Domagoj Markota (Fractional CTO) brings the technical and AI depth needed to make the platform genuinely useful. Daniela Hägg (Growth Associate) focuses on helping startups grow with clear priorities and better distribution.

We're Creatives Takeover Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales (Company No. 16741912). Our mission is simple: help people build startups from scratch with practical AI support, useful tools, and a founder-first ecosystem.

Got questions? Hit up javier@creatives-takeover.com or admin@creatives-takeover.com anytime.

How much does it cost and what do I get?

Rookie is free with 50 credits per month, 3 directory visits a month, and investor and accelerator browsing.

Starter is $9/month or $79/year with 100 credits per month. It adds a validation workspace for interviews and evidence, Email Templates, your MVP on your own domain, 5 VC profiles, 5 accelerator profiles, and 10 directory visits a month.

The core founder tools are on every plan and use credits where noted. Mentor marketplace access is shared too; mentor services are priced and paid separately. Accelerators, incubators and universities get custom pricing per program.

Can accelerators, incubators and universities use Creatives Takeover?

Yes. Programs can start with a 30 day founder validation pilot for 5 to 10 startups. We provide platform access, a structured validation workflow, weekly progress check ins and a final cohort report; the program provides the founders and one contact.

Staff see progress, not the content of founders' work, and founders keep their account, their work and the free plan after the program ends. A pilot does not promise product market fit, paying customers or investment readiness in 30 days. Pricing is set per program; see the Enterprise page to talk with us.

The Future Belongs to Creators

Building software has never been easier. AI can turn a prompt into research, design, code, and a working product in days. As the cost of building falls, output becomes less valuable as a competitive advantage. What matters more is judgment: knowing who you're building for, what they actually need, and what they'll pay for.

When building took a year, bad ideas often died before they reached the market because they never got finished. Now, anyone can build and launch in a week, giving weak ideas a much longer path to survive. They can reach customers, attract attention, and even get funded before anyone has established whether there is a real demand for them.

Creatives Takeover exists to help people make better bets. We work with creators, founders, and freelancers to understand the people they're building for, shape ideas around real needs, and bring products to life with purpose. The goal isn't simply to help more things get made. It's to help the right things get made.

Mission + Vision

Driven by purpose and guided by vision; discover what makes Creatives Takeover unique

Our Mission

Our mission is to empower anyone, anywhere, to launch their own startup by making advanced AI automation tools accessible, affordable, and easy to use.

We believe entrepreneurship should not be limited by technical skills, financial barriers, or location. By combining cutting-edge AI with intuitive workflows, we aim to streamline every stage of the startup journey, from idea validation and market research to branding, product development, and launch, so individuals can focus on innovation and creativity.

We envision a world where any person with an idea can bring it to life in record time, supported by intelligent automation that reduces costs, accelerates progress, and removes complexity. Through our platform, we strive to democratize startup creation and ignite a new wave of diverse, AI-powered businesses that drive economic growth and positive change.

Our Vision

Today, entrepreneurship is undergoing a fundamental shift driven by the rapid rise of AI. Recent advancements in generative AI, automation, and no-code tools are enabling founders to validate ideas, create products, and reach global markets at unprecedented speed and scale.

This evolution is dismantling the old barriers to entry and creating a new era where innovation is limited only by imagination, not resources.

We envision a future where entrepreneurship is as universal as ambition where anyone with an idea, regardless of background, education, or resources, can turn it into a thriving business. By fully unlocking the potential of AI automation, we aim to remove the barriers that have traditionally limited startup creation: high costs, technical complexity, and access to expert knowledge.

Founder questions answered

How long does it take to build a startup from idea to launch?

A focused founder can go from idea to first paying customer in 60–90 days: 2 weeks on ICP and validation, 6–8 weeks building an MVP, and 2–4 weeks on launch. The biggest time killers are skipping validation and overbuilding the first version.

Do I need a co-founder to build a startup?

No. Many successful startups were founded by solo founders. A co-founder reduces risk in specific areas (technical vs. business, for example), but the absence of one is not a reason to delay. Validate the idea first — then decide if you need a co-founder based on what the validation reveals.

How much money do I need to start a startup?

Idea validation costs almost nothing — 15 customer interviews and a landing page can be done for under $100. An MVP for a SaaS startup can often be built for $0 if you use free tiers of tools. The question to ask is: what's the cheapest way to prove the riskiest assumption?

What's the difference between a startup and a small business?

A startup is designed to test a hypothesis about a scalable business model — it's built to grow fast once the model is proven. A small business is designed to generate sustainable revenue from day one, usually in an established market. The tactics for each are very different.

Should I raise funding or bootstrap my startup?

Bootstrap if you can get to $10K MRR with your own resources — investors give better terms to founders who don't need their money. Raise if your business requires capital to compete (high CAC, hardware, regulated industries) or if the window for your market is short.

What is product-market fit and how do I know when I have it?

Product-market fit is when a specific customer segment regularly uses your product to solve a painful problem and would be genuinely upset if it disappeared. The Sean Ellis test asks: 'How would you feel if you could no longer use this?' If 40%+ say 'very disappointed', you likely have PMF in that segment.
